description: Task 4.3 Performance Optimization (HIGH). Reduce cloning and allocations on the hot event path, use references / Arc for shared data, and add pre-allocated buffers / interning where it measurably helps. Add a Rust benchmark harness (std-based, since cargo-flamegraph and criterion may be unavailable) and measure with the existing Python bench. Treat perf honestly: the known Python full-settrace overhead (~1200x) is inherent and the <10% target is not achievable for full tracing; optimize the hot paths that CAN be improved and report real numbers, not aspirational ones.
steps: Profile qualitatively by reading the hot path: xplainit-core/src/pipeline.rs, processor.rs, collector.rs, event_store.rs, sink.rs, formatter.rs, events.rs. Identify concrete unnecessary clones/allocations (e.g. cloning HashMaps/Strings/Vec<Value> when a reference or Arc would do, per-event String formatting that could reuse a buffer, repeated allocation of small collections).

Apply targeted optimizations that preserve behavior: pass borrows instead of cloning where lifetimes allow; wrap large shared/read-only structures in Arc to avoid deep clones; use Cow or &str where owned Strings were allocated needlessly; pre-allocate Vec/String capacity in hot loops (Vec::with_capacity); consider string interning for repeated function/module names if it is a clear win. Only change internals; keep public APIs and serialized output identical. Do NOT introduce a new external crate for this (offline sandbox) unless it is already in Cargo.lock.

Evaluate lock-free/parallel event processing: assess whether the existing event store/pipeline can use crossbeam (already a workspace dependency) channels or atomics to reduce lock contention. Only implement if it is a real, test-covered improvement; if it adds risk without measured benefit, document the evaluation and decline in a findings note rather than adding speculative concurrency.

Add a benchmark harness that runs offline: create xplainit-core/benches/ (or a bin/example) that constructs a large volume of events and times pipeline processing using std::time::Instant (no criterion unless it is already resolvable from Cargo.lock). Report throughput (events/sec) before/after in a docs/PERFORMANCE.md, with the exact measurement method and hardware caveat. Use xplainit-python/bench_overhead.py to capture the Python-side overhead number and record it honestly (do not claim the <10% target is met for full tracing).

Add revert-sensitive tests where optimizations change observable-but-stable internals: assert equality of serialized event output before/after (a golden test proving the optimization did not change semantics), and where an Arc/borrow refactor touches a public-ish path, add a test that would fail if a regression reintroduced a clone-related bug (e.g. shared-state mutation semantics). The benchmark itself is not a correctness test; ensure real assertions cover the refactored code.
Run the full gate set and the four Python suites. Commit on the branch: `refactor: performance - reduce cloning/allocations, add bench harness (FEAT-003)`.
acceptance_criteria: Concrete clone/allocation reductions are applied on the hot event path (Arc/borrow/Cow/with_capacity) without changing public APIs or serialized output.

A std-based offline benchmark harness exists and produces before/after throughput numbers recorded in docs/PERFORMANCE.md, with honest caveats (Python full-tracing overhead reported as-is, <10% target explicitly noted as not achievable for full tracing).
Any parallel/lock-free change is test-covered and measured, or explicitly declined with a documented rationale (no speculative concurrency).
Serialized event output is byte-for-byte unchanged (golden test) after the refactor.
Full gate set (build/test/clippy/fmt) passes and the four Python suites still pass.
Tests fail if a semantic-preserving optimization is reverted in a way that breaks output equality.
verification: cargo bench 2>&1 | head -40  (or run the example bench binary) to confirm the harness runs
source .venv/bin/activate && python test_automatic_tracing.py && cd xplainit-python && python bench_overhead.py
findings: Applied three behavior-preserving hot-path optimizations (public APIs and serialized JSON unchanged): (1) added ExecutionEvent::location_ref() -> Option<&SourceLocation> and switched PathFilter::should_capture (filter.rs) and AdvancedFilter/PerformanceFilter (advanced_filter.rs) to borrow the file path instead of cloning the whole SourceLocation; owned location() kept for API compat, with '<unknown>' fallback preserved for locationless variants; (2) MemorySink now uses VecDeque + pop_front (O(1) eviction) instead of Vec::remove(0) (O(n)); get_events() still returns an identically ordered Vec; (3) OutputFormatter::format_events writes into one pre-sized String instead of Vec<String>+join (byte-identical output). Offline std::time::Instant harness added at xplainit-core/examples/bench_pipeline.rs (no criterion/flamegraph needed; run: cargo run --release --example bench_pipeline -p xplainit-core). Measured before/after (N=200k, release, sandbox): path_filter.should_capture 21.8M->41.7M events/sec (~1.9x); memory_sink.write overflow 256K->7.33M events/sec (~28x); event_store.record / pipeline.handle_event / json.format_events unchanged within noise (expected: dominated by crossbeam queue push and serde_json which were not changed). Results + honest caveats recorded in docs/PERFORMANCE.md. CONCURRENCY: evaluated crossbeam channels / replacing the EventStats RwLock with atomics and DECLINED - EventStore already uses a lock-free ArrayQueue, record() is not lock-bound at these volumes, and Python-side cost dwarfs it ~1000x; adding concurrency would be speculative with no measured benefit (rationale documented in PERFORMANCE.md). HONESTY: xplainit-python/bench_overhead.py measured full-tracing overhead at ~1204.8x (+120,384%) over baseline (fib(24)); documented that the <10% target is NOT achievable for full call-granularity tracing (inherent CPython sys.settrace cost) - only selective tracing gets near a low budget. Revert-sensitive tests added in xplainit-core/tests/perf_regression.rs: byte-for-byte golden JSON (exact-string) test, exact FunctionExit JSON, location_ref-vs-location() equivalence for all variants, PathFilter decision parity incl. '<unknown>' fallback, and MemorySink FIFO overflow ordering. Golden events use <=1-key maps so serialization is deterministic (multi-key HashMap ordering is randomized per process). GATES: cargo build --release OK; cargo test 203 passed / 0 failed (up from 198, +5 new); cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings clean; cargo fmt --all --check clean. PYTHON: test_automatic_tracing 3/3, test_frame_filter 11/11, test_depth_accounting 23/23, test_decorators pass. Committed on branch phase4-production-hardening.
